warnings: Fix the primary visibility problem first: reframe or reposition the camera so the ball, impact point, and breach are clearly visible in the same shot.

If the particle system is intended to show secondary debris, Line 257 (`settings.render_type = NONE`) is likely suppressing visible output; switch to a visible render mode or instance debris geometry.

If the particle system is meant to add motion, Line 254 (`settings.physics_type = NO`) and Line 255 (`settings.normal_factor = 0.0`) leave particles with no physical launch; enable suitable physics or add initial velocity so debris actually travels outward from the impact.
Increase secondary debris density beyond Line 248 (`settings.count = 300`) if this system drives dust/chips; 300 is unlikely to sell a dense demolition burst.

The wall material needs to actually read as brick in render: verify the brick shader is applied to the fracture object, not overridden by a gray placeholder. Keep Line 319-320 brick colors only if they are visibly reaching the wall surface.
Model or simulate a real breach with broken silhouettes, varied fragment sizes, and surrounding cracks rather than a mostly intact panel.
Add volumetric dust and fine particulate debris around the opening so the air feels filled with demolition residue.
Improve environment context beyond the black void so the interior demolition location reads as a real building.
Use soft overcast lighting with enough exposure and contrast to preserve material readability without strong shadows.
Raise render quality/sampling or address shading issues causing wall banding.
